Changing a screen, explained

What a technician does when a screen is replaced. Knowing the steps helps you judge a quote, and helps you pick the right part.

  1. 1

    Check it really is the screen

    Lines, black patches, ghost touches or a dark screen with sound still working all point to the display, not the phone’s board.

  2. 2

    Warm the edges and lift the display

    Gentle heat softens the factory glue. A suction cup and thin picks open the phone without bending the frame.

  3. 3

    Disconnect the battery first

    The battery cable comes off before the screen cables, so nothing shorts while parts are moved.

  4. 4

    Move over the parts that stay

    The earpiece speaker and its sensor cable usually transfer to the new screen. On iPhones, True Tone needs the old screen’s data copied across with a programmer.

  5. 5

    Test before sealing

    The new screen is connected and tested for touch, brightness, colour and sensors before any glue goes on.

  6. 6

    Seal and check again

    Fresh adhesive keeps out dust and moisture. A last check makes sure the edges sit flush.

Inside a display assembly

Five layers, one part you replace

  1. Cover glass + touchLaminated to the panel in a display assembly.
  2. Display panelOLED / AMOLED or LCD — this is what the grade describes.
  3. Mid-frame“With frame” screens arrive already bonded to a new one.
  4. BatteryDisconnected first, before any screen cable.
  5. Back coverStays with your phone — not part of the screen.

Before you buy a screen

  • Match the exact model code

    Phones that share a name can use different screens. Check the code in Settings, About phone (for example SM-A546E), not just “A54”.

  • Pick the right grade

    OEM Original matches the factory screen exactly. OLED A Grade keeps deep blacks. Compatible A Grade is the budget choice for everyday use.

  • Need the fingerprint under the screen?

    In-display fingerprint readers only work through OLED and AMOLED panels. An LCD replacement won’t read your finger.

  • With frame or without

    A screen with the frame already fitted is faster and safer to install, especially on curved Samsung models, but costs a little more.

  • iPhone features to ask about

    Ask whether True Tone can be restored and whether a message about a non-genuine display will appear, so there are no surprises.

  • Warranty and testing

    Check the warranty length, keep the protective film on until the screen is tested, and keep your receipt for any claim.

How we grade a screen

Three grades, each tested before it is packed. The grade on the label is the grade in the box.

OEM Original

OLED A Grade

Compatible A Grade

OEM Original

The panel the phone maker fitted at the factory, supplied as a service part. Colour, brightness and touch match the original exactly.

OLED A Grade

A full OLED panel from an aftermarket line. True blacks and in-display fingerprint support on most models, at a lower price than OEM.

Compatible A Grade

Our best LCD or incell replacement. Every unit is powered on and touch-tested before it is packed.

What we stand for

Carefully selected grades

We stock a short list of suppliers per brand and reject batches that fail colour or touch checks. The grade on the label is the grade in the box.

Handled properly

Screens are stored flat in anti-static sleeves, shelved by model, and never stacked loose. Each one is logged from the moment it arrives.

Delivered safely

Rigid packing with corner guards for every courier parcel. If a screen arrives cracked, we replace it.
